body: Worker hand-over through the shim uses one exact marker line on the worker stdout (not forwarded): the shim stops feeding the old worker, closes its stdin, the worker drains every line already written, then leaves the hub (update_answer -> released) and exits 75; buffered Claude lines go to the next worker, which starts with the channel already initialized (env CCTG_WORKER_RESUMED). Rejected: replaying initialize in the shim (needs MCP parsing in the dumb shim) and exit-code-only switch (loses lines still in the pipe).

Restart request file is <state>/restart/<cctg run pid>.json, pid taken from env CCTG_RUN that cctg run sets for claude; rejected <session>.json (cctg run does not know the session id) and <claude pid>.json (an npm claude.cmd/node chain makes the child pid differ from the lineage pid).

Typed /exit is draft-safe: the worker types /exit, reads the input box between the last two rule lines, presses Enter only when it is exactly one line equal to the prompt glyph, U+00A0 or space, /exit; otherwise 5 Backspaces and answer draft_in_input. Rejected Ctrl+C / Esc Esc / Ctrl+U / Ctrl+S clearing (unverified; Ctrl+S restores an old stash on an empty prompt). Evidence p2.draft (draft submitted as a prompt), p2.safe_draft, p2.safe_idle.

Hooks carry only client_version (compile-time), not the binary hash: hooks are re-executed from the settings path on every event, so their hash equals the newest binary by construction and would cost a 9 MB read per hook; staleness is the long-lived worker build (sha256 of its exe) vs the hub build.

P1 said --settings changes are not picked up live, so claude restart is needed when a --settings/--mcp-config file named in CCTG_RUN_ARGS changed after the shim started (mtime > CCTG_SHIM_STARTED) or the shim level is below the worker requirement. Rejected tracking a settings hash in the hub (needs a first-registration snapshot and more wire).

Supervisor slimmed: candidate check, swap, trial watch and rollback move into cctg deploy; the supervisor keeps start/wait/backoff restart/Ctrl+C and restarts the hub on the request file cctg.restart, writing cctg.hub-started (pid and start nanos) at each start so deploy can watch the trial. Rollback still happens, but only while cctg deploy runs (it waits anyway).

cctg run ignores Ctrl+C/Ctrl+Break with a handler routine that returns TRUE, never SetConsoleCtrlHandler(NULL, TRUE): the NULL form is inherited by children and would stop claude from getting Ctrl+C (learn.microsoft.com setconsolectrlhandler).

First mutation set had two survivors because the reference code was redundant: an explicit U+00A0 replace (str::trim already strips it) and a `switching ||` guard in the shim (to_worker is None after the switch, so the line waits anyway). Both constructs removed; mutations replaced by meaningful ones (trim removed, buffered lines cleared) and update_e2e sends pings after `reloading` so they must pass through the shim buffer.

Restart relaunch arguments (drop the positional prompt per OPEN_DECISIONS Q4, drop session pickers, add --resume) are built by the updatable worker (update::relaunch_args, claude option table from claude --help 2.1.281) and written into the restart request; cctg run only runs the args of the request. Alternative rejected: a claude option table inside cctg run (not updatable, breaks the dumb-launcher rule).

Worker trusts CCTG_RUN only when that pid is the nearest ancestor of its claude before any other claude/node (update::launched_by over proctree::ancestors); otherwise ManualRestart. Alternative rejected: trusting the inherited env, which lets a claude started from inside another cctg run session send a restart into the wrong window.

Cut unused surface: UpdateOutcome::NoNewBinary, Client.restartable (hub never reads it), MIN_SHIM_LEVEL/old_shim (dead comparison; the CCTG_SHIM level env stays, so a future worker can add the check). Alternative rejected: keep them as seams (speculative, violates surgical-change rule).

Considered reading the input box before typing /exit (type only into an empty box, never Backspace). Rejected: an empty box can show placeholder text, which would make every restart refuse as a draft; the probed post-check (type, read, Enter only on exact /exit, else 5 Backspaces) stays.

Merge of main (TASK-042): heir() skips connections leaving after an update answer, so rebind() never hands a session back to a worker that is handing over. Alternative (keep heir as in main and rely on the leaving worker exiting fast) rejected: a failing new worker would rebind to the old one, contradicting 'leaving: bound to nothing'.

Verdict NEEDS_WORK on one targeted fix: run::channels_dialog takes the first '>'/U+276F line of the whole viewport, and after a same-window /exit the old claude frame ('❯ /exit' history line, empty input box) sits above the new dialog, so the dialog would be left unanswered. Fix: search only below the last 'Loading development channels' line. Alternative rejected: PASS with the risk documented, because it hits the acceptance item 'channels dialog answered' and the fix is two lines in the dumb launcher.

Worker copies in %TEMP% for crash restarts from the same build: every fresh copy costs ~0.5 s (debug exe ~1.2 s to initialize) because Windows scans the new file on first run; agent_stdio timing tests failed. Replaced by hard links next to the exe (0.017 s first run).

Shim runs each worker from a hard link <exe dir>/cctg-workers/<shim pid>-<gen>-<name> made at start and at hand-over; a crash restarts the same link, so a deploy is taken only via the press. Alternative rejected: hash check of the file on crash (no way to wait for a press without a worker) and a held open handle without delete sharing (would block deploy's rename of the same file).

minor-2: a press whose wait passes during a turn is kept until the turn ends and the topic is told once (UPDATE_WAITS_NOTICE). Alternative rejected: forget and ask to press again, because after a reload the agent is current and a second press answers 'already current', so a pending claude restart would be lost.

minor-7: the hub re-checks busy (hook-based, terminal turns included) when a Restarting answer arrives, right before it would send Released; if busy it does not release, keeps the agent bound, swallows the agent's later timeout 'failed' and asks again after the turn. Alternative rejected: worker-side screen check for a running turn (no stable busy marker on the 2.1.281 screen).
